status_summary: The removal tools the Foreword describes are in place: Schedule Policy/Career was reinstated by order on 2025-01-20, made at-will by OPM's final rule of 2026-02-06 and applied to listed positions by Executive Order 14410 of 2026-06-03 (see c03-01), and workforce reduction orders and an OPM reduction-in-force rule followed (see c03-06). Shuttering offices has begun with orders eliminating the non-statutory functions of eleven named entities in 2025 (see c03-09), while litigation over the placements is pending. The stage is derived from the three detailed records.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14171 signed; it redesignates the 2020 Schedule F framework as Schedule Policy/Career and has agencies petition OPM to place positions in it.
Executive Order 14210 directs agency workforce reduction plans, sets a limit of one hire per four departures and directs agency reductions in force.

Executive Order 14217 signed (published 2025-02-25): directs elimination of the non-statutory functions of four named entities (Presidio Trust, Inter-American Foundation, U.S. African Development Foundation, U.S. Institute of Peace).

Executive Order 14238 signed (published 2025-03-20): directs the same treatment for seven further entities, including the Federal Mediation and Conciliation Service, the U.S. Agency for Global Media, the Institute of Museum and Library Services and the Minority Business Development Agency.
Supreme Court (Trump v. AFGE, No. 24A1174) stays a N.D. Cal. injunction against Executive Order 14210, without ruling on specific reduction-in-force plans.
timeline.source: Supreme Court of the United States

timeline.event: OPM states that about 317,000 federal employees would leave in 2025, over 90 percent through voluntary programs.
OPM final rule on the Schedule Policy/Career framework published (effective 2026-03-09): covered positions stay career but are at-will, outside chapter 75 adverse-action procedures and MSPB appeals.

Executive Order 14410 signed (published 2026-06-10): places positions listed in an appendix in Schedule Policy/Career; press reports put the number at about 8,000 employees in more than 4,800 positions.
OPM final rule on reductions in force published (91 FR 49178), effective for notices issued on or after 2026-09-02.

title: Fire un-fireable career bureaucrats and shutter wasteful federal bureaus and offices
uncertainties: Stage derivation: c03-01 is implemented 75, c03-06 is implemented 75, c03-09 is in_progress 30. The two firing-side records would support implemented, but the Foreword also asks to shutter bureaus and the detailed record on cutting duplicated functions is only in_progress 30, so the combined stage is in_progress 60, the top of the band. Implemented 65 is defensible. c03-07 (political appointees) was left out of restates_ids because the sentence is about removing bureaucrats, and appears in related_ids and in c00-20. The copy of c03-09 was not in the folder; its stage comes from the existing listing and the two entity-closing orders were read on federalregister.gov in this run. The number of employees affected by Executive Order 14410 comes from press reports cited in c03-01, not from the order. The figure that about 317,000 federal employees would leave in 2025 is OPM's statement and includes voluntary departures, which are not removals. The Supreme Court stay is recorded as the court status; other suits are pending without rulings in the reports reviewed. c03-06 also records a narrower 2025-12-17 district court injunction on shutdown-period reductions in force (running through 2026-01-30), which is not repeated here; the court status reflects the Supreme Court stay of the broader injunction against Executive Order 14210.
